message.content:
Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component.

Score Step 4 of the SFCC-236 build (ZimmProductCardMedia molecule) — round 1. This is the most complex step so far; both Tester and Orchestrator found substantial real issues.

Files: overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts} + 1-import/1-entry diff in overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts.

## Orchestrator verdict: UNDER-scope
Everything else (badge, remove overlay, scroll-snap, ZimmSlideIndicator composition, AC1, alt text, loading, aspect ratio, wrap, single-image suppression, data-card-slot contract) fully delivered with concrete evidence. One specific gap: plan §4b says "assert the two never coexist in the same DOM" for arrows-vs-indicator — no test (DOM-based or structural-on-the-recipe) proves this, and the component's OWN test ("stamps every data-card-slot value when all optional slots are active") asserts BOTH `[data-card-slot="carousel"]` AND `[data-card-slot="indicator"]` are in the document simultaneously — the architecture is "both always in DOM, toggled by CSS `display` under a media query" (correctly avoids the opacity/visibility a11y anti-pattern per the Tester), consistent with how Step 6's plan spec ITSELF prescribes verifying equivalent hover-reveal claims later ("import the recipe object and assert... nested inside @media... gated") — but no such structural assertion exists here, and the DOM-presence claim as literally worded in the Step 4 criteria is not met. The Orchestrator judges the plan's own wording ("never coexist in the same DOM") was probably loose/pre-dated Step 6's more precise methodology, not that the architecture itself is wrong.

## Tester verdict: multiple CONFIRMED defects via real mutation testing

1. **🔴 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — same underlying issue as the Orchestrator's finding: mutation-proved zero regression coverage on the mutual-exclusivity mechanism. Deleted the entire `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` media-query gate from the recipe (arrows permanently visible regardless of pointer capability) — component's own 21 tests, recipeParts, recipeGuards, tsc, eslint, audit:tokens ALL still passed. This is because `index.test.tsx` mocks `useMultiStyleConfig` to `{}` for every part, so the real CSS is never exercised by any test.

2. **🔴 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — `close` and `arrowButton` recipe parts have ZERO `_focusVisible`/`_hover` styling. Both are real native `<button>` overlays sitting on top of photographic images with only the bare browser-default outline on keyboard focus. This breaks an established, 3-times-independently-verified codebase convention: `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`'s `pageButton`, `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`, and `zimmNavItem.css.ts` all apply the identical `outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)'` + `outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)'` pair via `_focusVisible`. No Figma citation exists either way on hover states specifically (unlike Step 2's SizeChip, where Figma explicitly enumerated 4 states with no hover/active) — this finding is about the UNIVERSAL focus-ring convention, not an invented hover treatment.

3. **🔴 CONFIRMED via fixture, ONE-OFF but real bug** — `currentIndex` state is never re-clamped when the `images` prop shrinks after the component is already mounted and navigated (e.g., a colour-variant swap that changes gallery length while the card stays on screen). Reproduced: navigate to last image of a 3-image gallery, re-render with a 2-image gallery, click "Next" — first click is a silent no-op (the internal `currentIndex` stays at the stale value 2), second click finally wraps correctly. `ZimmSlideIndicator`'s own display-side clamp masks this visually right after the shrink (shows "2 of 2", looks fine) but the component's OWN navigation math uses the stale unclamped value. Established precedent to copy exists in this exact codebase: `zimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own `useEffect` (cited in its own comments) clamps to the highest valid page when the offered set shrinks. This component's author clearly knows that precedent (referenced elsewhere in comments) but didn't apply it to `currentIndex`.

4. **🟡 CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** — the `scrollend` listener (`index.tsx:149-161`, real non-trivial clamping logic) has ZERO test coverage. Confirmed testable under jsdom (`container.dispatchEvent(new Event('scrollend'))` works; `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth` are definable properties even without real layout) — it just wasn't written.

5. **🟡 PLAUSIBLE, reasoned from confirmed code facts, not device-tested — a real WCAG 2.1.1 gap, distinct from finding #1/#2** — `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is a proxy for POINTER capability, not KEYBOARD presence. A device resolving this query false (touchscreen + physical keyboard, switch-access, or any `hover:none` desktop browser) gets: arrows `display:none` (unreachable), a non-interactive indicator (zero focusable content, confirmed by reading ZimmSlideIndicator's own source), and a scroll container with NO `tabIndex` and NO `onKeyDown` at all. There is currently no keyboard-operable way to page a multi-image gallery in that pointer profile — full stop. This is the single most novel and important finding: the mutual-exclusivity design conflates "show arrows vs. show indicator" with "keyboard operability vs. not," when it should be "visual affordance differs by pointer capability, but keyboard operability exists regardless."

## Your job

Score all six axes. This step has enough real, confirmed findings that a straight PASS seems unlikely — but weigh carefully what's authorized for THIS round vs. deferred:

- Finding #1/Orchestrator's UNDER verdict: same root cause. Fixable in-file by adding ONE structural test (import the real, unmocked recipe object; assert `carousel.display`/`indicatorWrapper.display` resolve to mutually-exclusive values under the media-query key) — this is exactly the technique the plan prescribes for Step 6's equivalent claim. Should this round also require reinterpreting/updating the plan's own Step 4 wording ("never coexist in the same DOM" → "never simultaneously visible/interactive, verified structurally") so it stops contradicting the architecture the rest of the build already commits to? That's a plan-doc edit, separate from a code fix — is it in your authority to direct, or should it be flagged for the orchestrating session to handle?
- Finding #2: cheap, safe, uses an existing universal token pair, zero design-invention risk (this is a mechanical a11y convention, not a Figma-sourced visual decision). Authorize as a fix.
- Finding #3: real, reproducible, has a precedent in-repo to copy. Authorize as a fix — but scope it tightly (add the clamp effect, don't restructure anything else).
- Finding #4: authorize adding test coverage for the scrollend listener, OR judge it acceptable to defer given time/scope pressure — your call, weigh against how load-bearing this logic is (it drives the touch-only indicator's accuracy, which was itself a hard-won accessibility requirement from earlier in this build per §4a).
- Finding #5: this is the big one. Is a full architectural redesign in scope for a REWORK round, or does this get reported to Marcel as a real, novel accessibility gap requiring a decision (e.g., "should the scroll container always be keyboard-operable via arrow keys regardless of pointer capability, as an additive, non-visual fix")? Consider: a MINIMAL fix (making the scroll container itself keyboard-operable — tabIndex, onKeyDown wired to the same navigation function the visible arrows already use — regardless of pointer capability) is purely additive, doesn't touch the existing visual hover/touch CSS split at all, and directly closes the WCAG gap. Is that minimal fix authorizable this round, or does even that need Marcel's sign-off first given it changes a documented architectural decision (§4a/§4b)?

Give PASS or REWORK. If REWORK, be SPECIFIC and BOUNDED — name exactly which findings get fixed this round, which get deferred/reported, and if you authorize the keyboard-operability fix, describe its minimal required shape precisely enough that the Implementer can't over-build it into something bigger.

content.text:
I read every touched file directly, located and read the cited precedent files (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`/`.tsx`, `zimmSlideIndicator/index.tsx`), and did not stop at reading — I ran independent falsification against the two highest-stakes claims rather than taking the Tester's word for them. Both reproduced. Full detail below.

## Independent verification performed

**Finding #1 (mutation survives all gates)** — backed up `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`, deleted the `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` media-query gate from both `carousel` and `indicatorWrapper` (arrows permanently visible), then ran `npx vitest run` on the component (21/21 passed), `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6/6 passed), and `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean). All green under the mutation. Restored the file and verified byte-identical via `diff`.

**Finding #3 (stale `currentIndex` on shrink)** — wrote my own probe (not copied from the Tester) into a backed-up copy of `index.test.tsx`: mount with 3 images, page to the last slide, `rerender` with 2 images while mounted, click "Next" once, assert the indicator reads "Image 1 of 2". It failed — the DOM after one click still read `aria-label="Image 2 of 2"`, proving the click was a silent no-op. Restored the test file, verified byte-identical via `diff`.

**Finding #2 (focus-visible)** — confirmed zero `_focusVisible`/`_hover` anywhere in `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`, and confirmed the cited convention exists identically in three other recipes (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:28-29`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts:47-49`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:174-176`), all using the exact `outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)'` / `outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)'` pair.

**Finding #4 (scrollend coverage)** — `grep -c scrollend index.test.tsx` = 0. Confirmed independently, not just accepted.

**Finding #5 (keyboard operability)** — confirmed in source: `scrollContainer` (`index.tsx:173`) has no `tabIndex`/`onKeyDown`; `ZimmSlideIndicator` (`index.tsx:58-72`) renders only a non-interactive `role="group"` div and `aria-hidden` segments — zero focusable content; `carousel` is `display:'none'` outside the same media query (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:142,149-151`).

**Baseline hygiene** — ran the full suite (760/760 passed, 50 files), `eslint` on the new folder (clean), and `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (repo-wide: one unacknowledged violation, and it's pre-existing/unrelated — `footer.css.ts:20`. This component's own `TAG_MIN_WIDTH = '78px'` is correctly in the tool's *acknowledged* list, its `audit-allow:` comment recognized as intended).

I also found a stronger precedent than the one cited to me: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts` and `.../zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` already exist in this exact repo, solving the exact same problem class ("index.test.tsx mocks useMultiStyleConfig globally, so these resolvers/gates are never exercised by any shipped component test") by importing the real recipe module and asserting on `.baseStyle()` output directly, no Chakra/DOM involved. This is a live, shipped pattern, not a forward-looking Step 6 promise.

## Axis scoring

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Correctness** | **FAIL** | Two 🔴 CONFIRMED defects (stale-index navigation bug; zero focus indicator on two real overlay buttons) — the rubric's PASS bar is explicit: "no 🔴 findings from the Tester," independent of green CI. `tsc`/`vitest`/`eslint` are otherwise clean — that's exactly what makes this a real gap, not a CI failure to chase. |
| **Completeness** | **FAIL** | Mutation-proven zero coverage on the mutual-exclusivity mechanism (D3); zero coverage on the `scrollend` clamp logic (D5); a reproducible functional defect in the shipped paging behaviour itself (D1). |
| **Pass criteria** | **FAIL** | Plan's own Step 4 wording ("assert the two never coexist in the same DOM") is unmet as written — the component's own test (`index.test.tsx:279-280`) asserts both slots ARE simultaneously in the DOM, which is the correct architecture but the opposite of the literal AC. |
| **Conformance** | **FAIL** | `close`/`arrowButton` break the established "every interactive overlay gets `_focusVisible`" convention, confirmed 3x elsewhere in this codebase. Structure/imports/registration/token-usage are otherwise clean. |
| **Restraint** | **FAIL** | Per this review's own governing rule: "An OVER or UNDER verdict fails this axis." The Orchestrator returned UNDER. (Flagging the tension: colloquially "restraint" reads as an over-build concern, and nothing here is over-built — but I'm applying the rule as written, not as I'd intuit it.) |
| **Design fidelity** | **UNVERIFIED** | No visual/Figma checkpoint was performed by anyone in this loop for this step, and I have no Figma file key for the cited nodes (40002742:46323/46322/46321, 40002536:7957) to check myself. Not a PASS — genuinely unknown. |

## Overall: REWORK (round 1 of 3)

## Answers to the scoping questions

**Finding #1 / plan wording** — the code fix (a structural test) is squarely in my authority to direct and is required this round; it's cheap, precedented twice already in this repo (see above), and directly closes both the Orchestrator's UNDER finding and the Pass-criteria gap. **The plan-doc wording edit is not mine to direct or make** — I could not locate any persisted Step 4/Step 6 plan document anywhere in the repo to even point to a line, which itself confirms this lives outside a reviewer's reach. Flag to Marcel/the orchestrating session: correct "never coexist in the same DOM" to something like "never simultaneously visible/interactive, verified structurally" — the architecture is right, the words describing it are stale.

**Finding #2** — authorized as a fix, scoped exactly as the Tester bounded it: `_focusVisible` only, on `close` and `arrowButton`. Do not add `_hover` — no Figma citation exists for a hover treatment on either element, and inventing one would itself be a Restraint violation.

**Finding #3** — authorized as a fix, scoped tightly: a clamp effect only, shaped after `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:75-84`'s precedent, plus a regression test.

**Finding #4** — I'm requiring it this round, not deferring: the marginal cost is low (the same test file is already being extended for D1/D3/D6), the logic is real branching/rounding math, it's confirmed testable under jsdom, and it's accessibility-load-bearing per the touch-indicator's own accuracy requirement. This is a judgment call, not a mechanical one — noting that explicitly rather than pretending it's obligatory.

**Finding #5** — I'm authorizing the minimal additive fix this round, not escalating it as a redesign, because it is purely additive, does not touch or reverse the §4a/§4b visual-affordance split, and closes a Level A WCAG 2.1.1 gap using only already-established primitives (the same focus-ring pair from D2, the existing `goToRelativeSlide` function, this file's existing `react-intl` pattern). Precise required shape, so it can't grow:
- `tabIndex={0}` on `scrollContainer`, gated on `totalSlides > 1` (same condition as the indicator — **not** `canPage`, so it still applies when `showControls={false}`).
- `onKeyDown` on the same element: `ArrowLeft` → `goToRelativeSlide(-1)`, `ArrowRight` → `goToRelativeSlide(1)`, `event.preventDefault()` on exactly those two keys (mirrors `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:109-111`).
- One new `defineMessages` entry (matching `previousImage`/`nextImage`) as `aria-label`, plus `role="group"` (matches `ZimmSlideIndicator`'s own choice).
- A `_focusVisible` outline on the `scrollContainer` recipe part, same `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` pair — mandatory consequence of making it focusable, not scope creep.
- One test mirroring the existing "arrows wrap" tests, fired via keydown instead of click.
- Explicitly out of scope: no change to `carousel`/`indicatorWrapper` CSS, no Home/End/PageUp/PageDown, no focus trap, nothing else.

Report to Marcel separately (not blocking): the arrows-vs-indicator model conflates visual affordance (pointer capability) with operability (input modality). This fix closes the immediate compliance gap; whether the Step 6 organism wants a more deliberate keyboard-first pattern is a design conversation, not a code defect.

## What I could not verify

Design fidelity (no Figma file key available this session — needs someone to screenshot `WithHoverSwap`/`MultipleImages`/`SingleImage`/`WithBadge` against the cited nodes); the exact real-device profiles that resolve `hover:none` while a physical keyboard is present (relying on documented CSS Media Queries L4 semantics, not a physical/BrowserStack test); the original plan document's full §4a/§4b context (not found in `.docs/` or anywhere else in the repo — my reading is from the quoted excerpts only).
